summary: BMAD-METHOD publishes no benchmark results for its own workflows; its quantitative statements are single release-note or doc lines without data: a catch-rate improvement of 50% to 100% at a 19% token cost per run for the Edge Case Hunter named-set pass (v6.10.0), the `bmad` skill handling over 80% of questions, 60-80% cost savings for web bundles, 59 known bugs (~25% of historical issues) for the reference validator, and a 91% npm tarball size reduction (6.2 MB to 555 KB). The bmad-eval skill ships a runner for baseline, variant, quality and trigger evals with committed cases for 2 skills and trigger queries for 8, but no run results are committed. The pass rates in docs/existing-codebases/theory-of-project-context.md (53% to 100%) come from cited third-party studies, not from runs of BMad.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
